name: hazel_weir_velocity_procedural_graph
description: Optimized Procedural Graph featuring 28-32 plot workforce-synchronized land scaling frozen at Day 16, integrated shed-dropoff-to-well transit loops, protected Strawberry compounding with selective rapid shop arbitrage, dynamic liquidation floors defended at >= 0.82x post-expansion, and strict 10-order engine cap order rationing.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand, total plot count, contiguous layout metrics, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks after hour 18 and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation with true livestock-scaled feed reserves (n_animals * 3) to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Fulfills active town shop contracts for 2.0x-3.5x premiums. Prioritizes existing shed inventory and rapid <= 4-day crops (Carrots and Potatoes, max 2-3 plots) while strictly barring 6+ day slow crops (Pumpkin, Cauliflower) after Day 5, ensuring >= 85-90% of land compounds hyper-fertilized Strawberries.

nodes.name: Capital Velocity & Liquidation
nodes.description: Executes continuous batch liquidations of unreserved, uncontracted surplus at dynamic price floors (>= 0.84x base normal; >= 0.78x midday hours 10-16 on expansion days <= 16 or when shed fullness >= 50%; defending >= 0.82x on mature days 17-28), capping liquidation orders at <= 3 slots per step to conserve order bandwidth within the 10-order engine cap.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Reads 96-step TTM forecast to dump sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) only when glut risk is acute (risk >= 0.52, price >= 0.82x base) before opponent dumping collapses market prices.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Reinvests surplus cash into synchronized workforce and land scaling across four waves (8-10 plots by Day 4-5 with 3-4 hands; 14-16 plots by Day 8 with 6-7 hands; 20-24 plots by Day 12 with 9-10 hands; 28-32 contiguous plots by Day 16 with 10-11 hands; hard land freeze at Day 16), decoupling daytime reinvestment (1.0x payroll) to accelerate hyper-fertilized Strawberry compounding with a Day 22 procurement cutoff.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with strict micro-dispatch sequencing: in-situ harvest-and-water recurring crops, shed drop-off paired with immediate well can refill transit loop, soil preparation and pre-seed hyper-fertilization, cluster harvesting, cluster watering, livestock feeding, and planting.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases; schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21; enforce emergency liquidation of unreserved, non-shop surplus inventory starting at hour 20 to guarantee payroll before midnight.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 3); never hoard phantom wheat when n_animals == 0; never liquidate crops committed to active town shop delivery; do not trigger emergency liquidation before hour 18 during normal daytime production.

attributes.condition: has_unlocked_shops and (shop_deliverable_inventory > 0 or (net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.25 + 50.0 and active_shop_demand > 0 and day <= 24)) and day <= 30
attributes.guidance: Allocate market slots to deliver exact matching inventory to town shops for 2.0x-3.5x premium through step 710. Prioritize immediate fulfillment from existing shed inventory (Strawberries, Milk, Wool, Carrots). For active high-premium (>= 2.0x base) contracts requiring new planting: 1) strictly require day + crop_growth_days <= contract_deadline and day <= 24; 2) permit fast crops only (Carrots and Potatoes, growth time <= 4 days) on at most 2-3 dedicated flexible plots; 3) strictly ban slow 6+ day single-harvest crops (Pumpkin, Cauliflower) after Day 5 to prevent cannibalizing 4+ recurring Strawberry flushes; 4) reserve exact shop quotas in shed so liquidation does not dump pending shop orders.
attributes.pitfalls: Never plant slow crops (Pumpkin, Cauliflower) after Day 5, as tying up plots for 7-8 days loses thousands in Strawberry flush compounding for a one-off premium. Do not ignore lucrative shop fulfillment for existing inventory or fast Carrots/Potatoes. Never buy shop seeds if net available cash is below 1.25x midnight payroll. Do not allow shop plot allocations to exceed 3 plots total.

attributes.guidance: Execute batch sales of unreserved, non-shop surplus holdings at dynamic price floors: maintain >= 0.84x base price during standard operations (shed < 50%). Permit sales down to >= 0.78x base price during midday reinvestment windows (hours 10-16) strictly on expansion days <= 16 to unlock fluid capital for land/seed scaling, or when shed fullness exceeds 50%. Defend a strict minimum liquidation floor of >= 0.82x base on mature compounding days (Day 17-28) to protect Strawberry profit margins. Cap batch sales at <= 3 market orders per step to preserve >= 7 order slots for reinvestment and shop fulfillment within the 10-order engine cap. Conduct terminal shed clearance strictly between steps 708-716 at a defended >= 0.74x floor.
attributes.pitfalls: Never dump bulk Strawberry harvests at sub-0.82x base price after Day 16 unless shed fullness exceeds 80%. Never consume more than 3 order slots per step for liquidation. Never sell Wheat below dynamic feed reserve (n_animals * 3). Never liquidate exact item quotas reserved for active town shop contracts. Avoid premature terminal fire-sales before step 708.

attributes.guidance: Preempt lowest-margin open orders; execute rapid batch liquidations of vulnerable commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) only when oracle_glut_risk >= 0.52 and current_price >= 0.82 * base_price before opponent dumping collapses market prices.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not front-run on hypersensitive or weak glut signals (risk < 0.52); never dump into collapsed sub-0.82 base price markets unless shed overflow is imminent; do not front-run commodities committed to active town shop contracts.

attributes.condition: ((hour < 18 and net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.0 + 50.0) or (hour >= 18 and net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.5 + 100.0)) and (hired_hands < 11 or (total_plots < 32 and day <= 16) or uncultivated_plots > 0 or has_fertilizer_deficit) and day <= 26
attributes.guidance: Scale workforce dynamically alongside contiguous land across four waves: reach 8-10 plots and 3-4 hands by Day 4-5, expanding to 14-16 plots and 6-7 hands by Day 8, reaching 20-24 plots and 9-10 hands by Day 12, and achieving 28-32 contiguous plots and 10-11 hands by Day 15-16 (~2.6-2.9 plots/hand). Enforce a hard land expansion freeze at Day 16, ensuring all late-planted Strawberries yield 4 full harvest flushes before Day 30. Decouple daytime reinvestment between hours 04:00-17:00 by requiring only 1.0x payroll reserve + action cost. Bootstrap Days 1-4 with Carrots, transitioning core acreage on Days 4-6 to hyper-fertilized Strawberries as cash flows allow. Enforce a hard Strawberry seed and fertilizer procurement cutoff at Day 22.
attributes.pitfalls: Never purchase plots after Day 16 as late land expansion cannot yield 4 harvest flushes and yields negative ROI. Never expand land when cash is below daytime reserve (1.0x payroll + plot cost before hour 18, 1.5x after hour 18). Never purchase Strawberry seeds or fertilizer after Day 22. Do not plant slow single-harvest crops on expanding acreage.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch hands following strict micro-dispatch priority: 1) In-situ Harvest & Immediate Water recurring crops (workers harvesting ripe Strawberry plots immediately water the plot in-situ if carrying water and plot is dry before departing), 2) Shed Drop-off & Central Well Refill Loop (deposit goods at shed when backpack full or hour >= 20; immediately top off watering can to 100% capacity at central well before exiting transit loop to fields), 3) Soil Preparation & Pre-Seed Hyper-Fertilization (apply fertilizer to tilled soil before seeding to ensure all Strawberry plots are hyper-fertilized), 4) Cluster Harvest adjacent ripe plots up to backpack capacity, 5) Cluster Watering of any remaining dry cultivated plots to eliminate regrowth halts, 6) Livestock Feeding (maintain feed reserve: n_animals * 3), 7) Planting seeds (hyper-fertilized Strawberries primary on >= 85-90% acreage; max 2-3 dedicated plots for active fast shop crops), 8) Till/Weed new plots.
attributes.pitfalls: Never allow Strawberry plots to remain unwatered post-harvest, as dry intervals freeze regrowth clocks. Never send workers into fields with empty watering cans; always refill can at central well upon completing shed drop-off. Never plant Strawberry seeds on unfertilized plots; always apply fertilizer prior to seed placement. Never create dispatch deadlocks if an action cannot be performed immediately; gracefully fall through priority chain. Ensure no hand idles while harvestable crops or dry plots exist.
